skills.name: Fundamentals: scale of preference and opportunity cost

note.text: A scale of preference ranks wants in order of importance to a decision maker. Choice depends on this ranking and on available resources. Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative forgone, not all rejected alternatives added together. It can involve time or an activity rather than money. A monetary cost is an amount paid; it need not measure the full opportunity cost. State what was actually given up and what the decision maker would otherwise have chosen.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A scale of preference ranks wants in order of importance to a decision maker. Choice depends on this ranking and on available resources. Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative forgone, not all rejected alternatives added together. It can involve time or an activity rather than money. A monetary cost is an amount paid; it need not measure the full opportunity cost. State what was actually given up and what the decision maker would otherwise have chosen.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Ngozi ranks repairing her school bag above buying a novel, and the novel above buying a bracelet. If she can afford only one, choosing the repair gives up the novel as the next-best alternative. The bracelet is also not bought, but it is not added to the opportunity cost. If she later receives more resources, the feasible set can change without changing the meaning of opportunity cost.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: List feasible alternatives, rank them and identify the best rejected option. Do not confuse the chosen benefit with what is forgone. If an exercise asks for a remaining balance, subtract spending from the available budget and keep CFA francs in the answer.

key_words.meaning: a ranking of wants in order of importance
the next-best alternative forgone by a choice
the amount paid for a purchase
the resource limit on affordable choices

examples: Bih places school-bag repair above a novel and a bracelet.
Bih chooses bag repair; the novel was her best rejected option.
A trader pays for a notebook.

mistake.wrong: A preference ranking lists all items as equally important.

mistake.why: A scale of preference shows priority, rather than an unranked list.
